title: Spike: copy a film's image subtitles without reading the whole film
description: D-003 accepted one whole-film read per film version to copy its image tracks, and the .sup copy reads the film once per track. The scan already keeps the image tracks' cue points (media_sources.image_cues, DOMAINS 51). Can the tracks be copied by ranged reads at those points instead, and for which films?
acceptanceCriteria: For Matroska films with Cues for the subtitle track, and for those without: whether ranged reads at the stored cue points copy every packet of the track, measured against today's whole-film copy (bytes read, time, packets equal)
The same answer for the .sup copy
The same answer for text-track extraction, which today also reads the whole film (it decides what JS-091's background extraction would cost)
A recommendation with what each kind of film would then cost, recorded in spikes/; a follow-up task if it works
source: decision D-003; product-owner direction review 2026-11-19 (no further whole-film-read trade-off until it reports)
notes: D-070: a 4K HDR re-encode ran 16% to 18% slower for as long as its worker's PGS copy ran (JS-177's spike), and 0.85x to about 0.6x on the dogfood (JS-154). Moves to directly after JS-177 on: the own-extraction slow-job reason counted on the dogfood more than twice in a week; an operator report of it; or JS-143's count showing more than a few image-track reads a week. Dropped (D-126 and the pivot, D-107): Rule 14, and JS-188 first. Moved to the backlog (D-127).
